newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco silver mine offer oversubscribed 5.8 times.
newsitem.headline: Morocco silver mine offer oversubscribed 5.8 times.

text.p: Public offering for sale of the state's 20 percent stake in Morocco's Imiter silver mine was 5.87 times oversubscribed, Privatisation Minister Abderrahmane Saaidi said on Wednesday.
Early in June, the privatisation ministry floated 20 percent of Imiter worth 130.3 million dirhams ($13.7 million), or 396 dirhams per share. The offer closed on June 13.
"The public offering for sale of the 20 percent stocks in Imiter was a real success. The 329,018 shares offered were oversubscribed 5.87 times," Saaidi told a news conference.
Among the 14,153 bidders for the sale were 14,033 individuals and 120 institutional investors, including foreigners representing 7 percent of the would-be buyers, the minister said.
Holders of privatisation bonds (certificates) who bid for the sale were all satisfied, the minister said.
"It was the first operation to convert privatisation bonds in 1997," Saaidi said.
It was the 12th flotation on the bourse since the government launched its privatisation programme in 1993, a broker said.

The state had been holding a stake of 33 percent of Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter (SMI) through the state-run Bureau des Recherches et Participation Minieres (BRPM). The remaining 67 percent of the capital is owned by Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA group.

Saadi said the state has earned 5.01 billion dirhams ($533 million) in the fiscal year 1996/97 from the sale of state-owned equities, bringing the state total earnings to about 14 billion dirhams ($1.5 billion) since privatisation began in 1993.
